subject: Post-call: Aurora Labs reserved GPU qualification & SLA targets
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chang <emily@auroralabs.com>, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@auroralabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 16:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-call: Aurora Labs reserved GPU qualification & SLA targets

Thanks again for your time today — great conversation. Quick recap from my side so we have a single source of truth and clear next steps. Please reply with any corrections.

Summary of pain points you described:
- Large p95 latency spikes during east-coast peak windows (11:00–15:00 ET) impacting interactive search and summarization flows.
- Multi-tenant tail-latency variance when batch jobs overlap with real-time inference.
- Regulatory constraint: subset of traffic (PHI) must be isolated to customer-dedicated hardware.

Goals we agreed on:
1) Isolation: reserved pool for PHI workloads with strict tenancy separation and audit logs.
2) SLOs: initial target p95 latency <= 250ms for short prompts (<256 tokens), 99.9% availability for the reserved pool.
3) Throughput: support steady-state ~120 req/s with 95th percentile spikes to ~220 req/s during batch processing windows.
4) Cost/ops: predictable monthly commit, plan for staged burst capacity during release windows.

Proposed dedicated capacity and scaling plan (initial recommendation):
- Stage 1 (Pilot / 30d): 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs in a dedicated pool (isolated tenancy).
- Prefix/KV caching enabled for repeated prompts to reduce token compute.
- Autoscale guardrails: allow burst to 12 GPUs (pre-warmed) for up to 6 hours/day around releases; fall back to hosted compatible model variant if sustained usage exceeds burst.
- Quantization profile: int8 quantization for non-PHI routes to reduce cost; keep FP16 for PHI model variant during pilot.

SLA & operational checks:
- SLO: p95 latency <= 250ms for <256-token requests; target throughput and error budget to be captured in MOP.
- Observability: token-level cost/latency dashboards + per-route tracing; we will provide a shared dashboard.
- Security: we will supply SOC2 artifacts and KMS integration checklist.

Attachments I’m including from today: aurora_mop_v1.pdf (initial MOP draft) and aurora_qps_sample.csv (sample QPS profile you dropped into the call).

Immediate next steps (mutual action plan):
- Emily/Tom: confirm the QPS sample is representative of a typical week or share a 7-day sample (action: Emily) — due 2026-05-15.
- Redwood: schedule a technical deep-dive with infra engineers to validate kernel/sequence-length tradeoffs (action: Ben) — target week of 5/18.
- Legal/Procurement: we’ll share a draft MSA and pricing term sheet; you’ll confirm procurement cadence (action: Soojin/Hannah) — initial MSA link below.
- Agreement checkpoint: sign pilot committed capacity for 8 GPUs and a 30-day pilot by 5/22.

If that looks right, reply “ACK” with any timing adjustments and we’ll lock the technical call.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai]
[Attachment: aurora_mop_v1.pdf (PDF, 84KB)]
[Attachment: aurora_qps_sample.csv (CSV, 12KB)]

From: Emily Chang <emily@auroralabs.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@auroralabs.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Aurora Labs reserved GPU qualification & SLA targets

Hannah — thanks for the clear write-up. This matches our notes closely. A couple clarifications: 
1) The 120 req/s is per-region steady-state (US east + US west combined are ~200 req/s steady during weekdays). The sample you have was only east traffic; I’ll send a combined week snapshot by Friday.
2) For PHI isolation, we need a hard tenancy boundary (no shared kernels) — not just v-net separation. Can you confirm Redwood’s isolation model supports that?

ACK on the pilot timeline; sign-off on 8 GPUs for 30 days makes sense as a first step. We’ll also want a short runbook on failover behavior if the reserved pool hits sustained >12 GPU-equivalent demand.

— Emily
Emily Chang
Head of ML Platforms, Aurora Labs
emily@auroralabs.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Post-call: Aurora Labs reserved GPU qualification & SLA targets

Looping infra/ops on Emily's tenancy ask. Technical notes for the deep-dive: 
- Isolation: we can provision a dedicated pool with GPU-level tenancy (no shared kernel instances) and HSM-backed KMS for keys. Will need legal sign-off for audit scope.
- Latency: p95<=250ms looks feasible for their short prompts on 8xA100 if we enable continuous batching with strict latency buckets and reserve a small headroom for preemption.
- Burst: pre-warm nodes for burst to 12 GPUs; if sustained beyond 6 hours we should have a policy to reroute a % of lower-priority traffic to a cheaper quantized variant.

Action for me: propose two configuration options for pilot (costed):
A) 8xA100 dedicated, FP16, pre-warm 4 GPUs for burst (cost estimate X)
B) 8xA100 dedicated, FP16 for PHI / int8 for non-PHI routes with autoscale to 12 for bursts (cost estimate Y)

I’ll have a draft config + ops playbook before the deep-dive.

— Ben

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chang <emily@auroralabs.com>, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@auroralabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 15:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Aurora Labs reserved GPU qualification & SLA targets

Thanks Emily — appreciate the quick clarify. Two small updates based on Ben’s notes: 
- Confirmed: Redwood supports GPU-level tenancy (we’ll include the detailed isolation spec in the MOP).
- We’ll draft the failover runbook you requested — it will outline graceful degradation, model fallback percentage, and a notification cadence.

Next concrete items before our tech deep-dive: 
1) Emily: send combined 7-day QPS profile (due 2026-05-15).
2) Soojin: share draft MSA & pricing stub, and open the DocuSign room for the pilot (Soojin to confirm).
3) Ben: share pilot configuration options A/B with cost estimates by 5/17.
4) Hannah: schedule deep-dive for week of 5/18 and send calendar invite.

I’ll also add the HubSpot deal link and the preliminary DocuSign room for the MSA in a follow-up. If there are no objections, I’ll book the deep-dive for Tuesday 5/19 10:00 PT.

Thanks all — Hannah
